title: Provenance addendum for qumode_qsk_gpu (does not modify PROTOCOL_FROZEN.json)

protocol_hashes.note: Two hashes are in circulation and must not be conflated. The file SHA-256 is of the exact bytes of protocol/PROTOCOL_FROZEN.json. The embedded protocol_sha256 is SHA-256 of the sorted compact JSON with the protocol_sha256 key removed. Neither was recomputed by rewriting the file.

starts_py.note: cpu_oracle/src/starts.py is a write-guarded copy, not byte-identical to the campaign file. Only pack_panel_starts changed (it now requires an explicit out_dir so it cannot write into the live campaign tree). spsa_starts / all_starts / freeze_cell_starts recipes are unchanged.

protocol_source_pins_predate_audited_cod.note: PROTOCOL_FROZEN.json source_pins were written 2026-11-10 20:22 +08, before later campaign edits. The gpu cpu_oracle snapshot is the live audited CPU code as of the GPU tree build, which postdates those pins. This addendum documents the mismatch; the frozen protocol file is not edited.
protocol_source_pins_predate_audited_cod.audited_and_ported_jacobian: reverse-mode, cross-checked against forward-mode and FD in the CPU campaign audit

fixture_producer.note: Fixture run JSONs (SPSA/BFGS/entropy results copied from the live MAIN campaign) do not carry source pins or a compiler timestamp that would prove which hamiltonian.py version produced each trajectory. The producer is therefore not proven from the bundle. This is labelled honestly; fixture history is not silently repaired.
fixture_producer.scientifically_bounded: E and F at a stored x depend only on the state map, which is the same in the later reverse-mode CPU code and this port. The gradient implementation affects only the trajectory that produced x. GPU gradients are compared against the bundled cpu_oracle, not against stored fixture gradients (those were not kept on disk).

campaign_library_versions_on_authoring_b.note: Read from the same machine that was running the CPU campaign at review-revision time (python3 import). The GPU host should install these exact versions so SciPy BFGS and NumPy RNG match the campaign. They are recorded in the GPU_TEST_PASS binding and in each result.
campaign_library_versions_on_authoring_b.enforcement_note: The production gate and GPU_test refuse unless python/numpy/scipy/numba equal these strings, unless an explicit --allow-version-drift is recorded (stamp and results are then unofficial). Added after review round 2; the pin values themselves are unchanged.

fma_and_reductions.note: Stock CuPy elementwise may FMA-contract; RawKernels are compiled with --fmad=false. libm exp/cos/sin and reductions can still differ at ULP level, so bitwise CPU parity is not promised. Batch-2 vs batch-1 energy reductions of the same x can also differ at ULP level.
